steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That logic doesn't work. Killing everyone doesn't prove your innocence.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: When you're the only one left... Hilda wouldn't see a savior. She'd see the most likely suspect.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: No... that's not true! I'm her most trusted subordinate! She would believe me!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Do you really think she'd trust the person who slaughtered all the other people?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You'd have a better chance if you let me live. I can vouch for you.
You turn, a slow and deliberate motion. The blade bites deep, slicing through cloth and skin, but you refuse to flinch. Your eyes lock directly with Nolaine's, meeting her gaze with unwavering calm.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I believe you. Someone willing to go this far to ensure Hilda's survival... couldn't be the mole.
The knife in Nolaine's hand begins to betray a tremor.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: Hilda... has to live... Monolith... is the city-state's only hope...

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: I have to... I must protect her!! No matter what!!

You make a grab for Nolaine's knife. The hilt leaves her grip, but it's a feint. Using the momentum, she spins, wrist flicking to reclaim the blade in a fluid, deadly arc aimed at your ribs. Simultaneously, her other hand claws for the gun in your grasp.
Instinct takes over. You lock onto her arms, muscles straining as you wrench them away. A frantic, brutal twist, and then, the muffled, sickening thump of the trigger being pulled.
She crumples. And as her body meets the ground, your gaze lifts to the doorway. Hilda stands there, frozen.
After all this time together, you've learned to read the subtle shifts beneath her icy composure.
Her eyes are wide, not just with shock, but a scalding disappointment. And beneath it all, a raw, unmistakable pain of betrayal.
The barrel of her gun rises, steadying on you.
Innocence is a lost cause. There is no proof, only the damning scene she witnessed. But you still have one decision to make—
